title: Command card
description: One terminal command, explained flag by flag. They will paste it without reading it, so it has to be correct standing alone.

command.description: The command as typed. Mark anything they must substitute with angle brackets, e.g. <branch-name>, so it is never pasted literally by mistake.

tool.description: git, gh, cargo, npm, pnpm, claude, codex, winget

flags.description: Every flag that is not self-evident. The reader does not know what -u does, and nobody ever tells them.

destructive.description: True for anything that can lose work: reset --hard, push --force, clean, rm, checkout --. The linter requires `danger`, `destroys`, and `safer_first` whenever this is true.

destroys.description: Exactly what is lost, and whether it is recoverable. 'There is no undo' when there is no undo.

safer_first.description: The command to run before this one to make it survivable. Usually `git stash` or a backup branch.

undo.description: How to reverse it, or the honest statement that you cannot.

expect.description: What success prints. Following rule 4 of the authoring guide: every instruction gets a verification step.
